title: Earned value
intro: Every formula starts with EV. A variance subtracts, an index divides. A negative variance or an index below 1.0 is bad news. The examples use BAC 200,000, PV 100,000, EV 80,000 and AC 90,000.

entries.name: Planned value, earned value, actual cost
entries.formula: PV: budget of the scheduled work. EV: budget of the work actually done. AC: cost actually incurred.
entries.reading: BAC is the sum of all budgets for the work. Total PV is the performance measurement baseline.
entries.section: Earned value management and the baseline

entries.name: Cost variance
entries.reading: Negative: over planned cost. Positive: under.
entries.section: Variances and indices

entries.name: Schedule variance
entries.reading: Negative: behind schedule. Positive: ahead.
entries.section: Variances and indices

entries.name: Cost performance index
entries.reading: Below 1.0: over planned cost. Each dollar spent earns CPI dollars of work.
entries.section: Variances and indices

entries.name: Schedule performance index
entries.reading: Below 1.0: behind schedule
entries.section: Variances and indices

entries.name: Estimate at completion, current CPI continues
entries.reading: The typical case
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Estimate at completion, rest at the planned rate
entries.reading: The variance was a one-off
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Estimate at completion, plan no longer valid
entries.reading: Reestimate the remaining work
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Estimate at completion, CPI and SPI both count
entries.reading: Cost and schedule performance both affect the remaining work
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Estimate to complete
entries.formula: ETC = EAC − AC, or a bottom-up reestimate
entries.reading: The cost to finish the remaining work
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Variance at completion
entries.reading: Negative: the project will end over budget
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: To-complete performance index
entries.formula: TCPI = (BAC − EV) ÷ (BAC − AC), or ÷ (EAC − AC) once an EAC is approved
entries.reading: Work remaining ÷ funds remaining. Above 1.0: harder to complete.
entries.section: Forecasting: EAC, ETC, VAC and TCPI

entries.name: Earned value in agile
entries.formula: EV = completed story points × cost per point; PV = planned story points × cost per point
entries.reading: No partial credit: a story counts only when the customer accepts it
entries.section: EVM in agile and hybrid projects

entries.name: Three-point estimate, triangular
entries.reading: Simple average of optimistic, most likely and pessimistic. Used with little historical data.
entries.section: Estimating durations with benchmarks and history

entries.name: Three-point estimate, beta (PERT)
entries.reading: Weighted average: the most likely value counts four times
entries.section: Estimating durations with benchmarks and history

entries.name: Three-point cost estimate
entries.reading: The same formula for costs
entries.section: Estimating costs

entries.name: Cost baseline and project budget
entries.formula: Work estimates + contingency reserve = cost baseline; cost baseline + management reserve = project budget
entries.reading: Contingency is for known risks, inside the baseline. Management reserve is for unknown-unknowns, outside it.
entries.section: Building the budget and planning spend tracking

entries.name: Estimate accuracy
entries.formula: Rough order of magnitude: −25% to +75%. Definitive: −5% to +10%.
entries.reading: Accuracy improves as more is known. The definitive range is the Sixth Edition's; the estimating standard gives −10% to +15% for later estimates.
entries.section: Estimating costs

title: Schedule
intro: These formulas start the project on day 1, as the lesson does. Courses that start on day 0 drop the − 1 and + 1.

entries.name: Early finish (forward pass)
entries.reading: The earliest an activity can finish
entries.section: Creating the schedule: the critical path

entries.name: Late start (backward pass)
entries.reading: The latest an activity can start without delaying the project
entries.section: Creating the schedule: the critical path

entries.name: Total float
entries.formula: Total float = LS − ES = LF − EF
entries.reading: Zero on the critical path, the longest path. Negative float: a constraint forces dates earlier than the logic allows.
entries.section: Creating the schedule: the critical path

entries.name: Average velocity
entries.formula: Points of accepted stories ÷ number of iterations
entries.reading: Plan from the average of recent iterations. Specific to one team: never compare teams.
entries.section: Release forecasting

entries.name: Iterations needed
entries.formula: Remaining story points ÷ average velocity, rounded up
entries.reading: When scope is added, the forecast moves out
entries.section: Release forecasting

entries.name: Flow metrics
entries.formula: Lead time: request to delivery. Cycle time: start of work to finish. Throughput: items finished per period.
entries.reading: Lead time includes the wait before work starts. Limiting WIP exposes bottlenecks.
entries.section: Tracking progress: burn charts and flow metrics

entries.name: Weighted shortest job first
entries.formula: WSJF = (business value + time criticality + risk reduction) ÷ size
entries.reading: The highest score goes first
entries.section: Prioritizing work by value and feedback

entries.name: Cost of delay divided by duration
entries.reading: Prioritizes by time sensitivity and economic impact
entries.section: Prioritizing work by value and feedback

entries.name: Communication channels
entries.reading: N is the number of people, including the project manager. Read whether the question asks for the total or the number added.
entries.section: Communication channels

entries.name: Probability-impact score
entries.reading: The highest scores get attention first
entries.section: Qualitative risk analysis

entries.name: Expected monetary value
entries.reading: Threats negative, opportunities positive
entries.section: Quantitative risk analysis

entries.name: Decision tree
entries.formula: EMV of each option = the sum of probability × outcome over its branches
entries.reading: Choose the option with the larger EMV. In the lesson's example, upgrading (46) beats building a new plant (36).
entries.section: Quantitative risk analysis
